findings: H1 confirmed. At server/internal/service/task_knowledge.go:350-360, BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim refuses any v1 claude invocation whose inv.ExtraArgs or agent custom_args fail validateTaskKnowledgeOrdinaryArgs. That check is the admission allowlist agent.ValidateKnowledgeSessionArgs (pkg/agent/knowledge_launch.go:104-135, five flags, default branch refuses) plus --no-session-persistence. The refusal runs before the gate is consulted at line 366, so it fires with MULTICA_KNOWLEDGE_CONTEXT_ENABLED unset.

The daemon cannot avoid H1. internal/daemon/knowledge_context.go:93-118 attaches inv, including defaultArgsForProvider (MULTICA_CLAUDE_ARGS) as ExtraArgs, to every claim from an mdt_ credential. It has no view of the server gate.

What the code already treats as session selectors. buildClaudeArgs (pkg/agent/claude.go:830-845) emits --resume itself, then appends ExtraArgs and CustomArgs through filterCustomArgs. claudeBlockedArgs (claude.go:777-790) holds only -p, --output-format, --input-format, --permission-mode, --mcp-config and --effort, plus --settings when a settings path is managed. So a user selector such as --continue reaches argv after unshellQuoteArg strips one layer of quotes; '--continue' becomes --continue.

Other selector lists. collaborationrun/host_config.go:61-67 denylists --resume, -r, --continue, --session, --session-id, --fork-session (plus cross-provider --attach/--server/--url/--cwd/-C/--directory/--workdir/--config-dir/--model/-m), any -r* short form, and claude '-c' only as an exact token. It misses clusters such as -pc or -cr, and quoted forms. grok.go:40-51, pi.go:618-630 and qwen.go:37-39 block -r/--resume, -c/--continue, --session-id and --fork-session for their providers. The leaf test TestKnowledgeEffectiveArgsCannotOverrideSessionSelection (pkg/agent/knowledge_launch_test.go:402) lists the forms the allowlist must refuse.

The leaf contract matches base execution. TestKnowledgeAmbiguousLegacyContinueRefused (knowledge_launch_test.go:476-500) shows that with opts.Knowledge == nil, ordinary execution keeps --continue unstripped. prepareKnowledgePrompt (knowledge_context.go:294-297) returns the plain prompt when task.KnowledgeContext is nil. A nil descriptor from the server is therefore a working ordinary path.

In the unsupported branch (task_knowledge.go:367-381), the history guard already refuses three cases: a retained negotiated row, any prepared non-empty exposure in the runtime/daemon/owner namespace, and corrupt or >128-row history. What it cannot see is exposure whose task rows were deleted, or a transcript that an explicit selector reaches. That gap is why selector refusal must remain an independent rule.

M1 confirmed. server/internal/handler/daemon.go:3234-3241 maps every non-*service.CollaborationError from BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim to knowledge_unavailable and calls failClaimedTaskBeforeLaunch, which settles the task as failed. knowledge_unavailable is not in retryableReasons (service/task.go:5267-5274). BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim runs on every claim and always reads ListTaskKnowledgeRuntimeHistory on the unsupported path (codex, legacy, gate off).

The neighboring transient handling in the same builder requeues immediately with TaskService.RequeueTaskAfterClaimFailure and returns a 500 claimBuildFailure: agent load at daemon.go:2214-2225 and source-context load at daemon.go:3106-3112. Both keep pgx.ErrNoRows terminal (daemon.go:2199-2213; rejectClaimSourceLoad at 1980-2001).

Requeue is safe for knowledge state. RequeueAgentTaskAfterClaimFailure (pkg/db/queries/agent.sql:946-963) resets only status, dispatched_at, prepare_lease_expires_at and delivered_comment_ids, guarded by a CAS on claim_generation and dispatched_at. knowledge_context_version and knowledge_delivery are untouched, so no recorded exposure is lost or relabeled. BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim discloses nothing and finalizes nothing.
The batch claim handler (daemon.go:1869-1876) skips any task whose builder returned a failure, so the M1 fix needs no change there.
root_cause:
H1: commit 96cedf485 reused the admission allowlist as the refusal rule at claim time. ValidateKnowledgeSessionArgs was written to prove that a knowledge launch is fully controlled, so it refuses everything it does not know. BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim applies it before the gate or support decision, so "not provably controlled" became "refuse the task" even when no negotiation will happen. The spec reserves refusal for selectors that could recover managed history, and for proven or unprovable exposure.

M1: the claim handler treats every error that is not a CollaborationError as a knowledge-domain refusal. Infrastructure failures (pgx and connection errors, context deadlines) therefore get the same terminal, non-retryable settlement as a genuine fail-closed knowledge decision. This happens on a path that runs for every claim.

Every other option goes through the existing support decision. The allowlist stays the only admission rule, so an unlisted or no-persistence option means unsupported, and the existing history guard chooses between base execution and refusal.

The token scan is deliberately coarse, so some harmless values (for example '-x=bar') refuse. Current code refuses those too, so this is no regression. chosen:
H1-A plus M1-A.

H1 rule. Selector detection, KnowledgeSessionSelectorPresent("claude", args): scan every token, including values and tokens after "--", with no arity parsing. Unquote each token with unshellQuoteArg, exactly as buildClaudeArgs does, then take name = the part before the first "=". A token is a selector when either:
1. name starts with --resume, --continue, --session, --fork-session or --from-pr. This covers --resume=x, --resume x, --resume-session-at, --session-id, --continue=true and '--continue'.
2. the token is a single-dash short cluster (starts with "-", not "--") whose characters after the dash include 'c' or 'r'. This covers -c, -r, -rID, -cr and -pc.

These are the only args treated as able to recover managed history. Everything else is an ordinary option: --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --add-dir, --model, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd, --verbose, --settings, --append-system-prompt, --debug, and also --no-session-persistence, which disables persistence and selects nothing.

Decision matrix. It applies only to v1 invocations (inv.ProtocolVersion == 1) on a claude runtime, to both inv.ExtraArgs and agent custom_args, and is the same with the gate on or off:
- Any selector, or custom_args JSON that does not decode: refuse with knowledge_invocation_unsupported before launch. The selector is never stripped. This is the current behavior, kept.
- Gate off and no selector: unsupported. The existing history guard decides. A retained negotiated row or exposure in the namespace is refused; corrupt or >128-row history gives knowledge_context_changed; otherwise the claim returns a nil descriptor and the chosen pointer unchanged (ordinary base execution). This is where the defect is fixed.
- Gate on, no selector, all args inside ValidateKnowledgeSessionArgs, and no --no-session-persistence: negotiate as today.
- Gate on, no selector, any other option (for example --allowedTools) or --no-session-persistence: unsupported, then the same history guard. A fresh unexposed task runs base execution and never negotiates. A retained negotiated task refuses.
- inv == nil (legacy daemon) or a non-claude runtime: unchanged.

The leaf check in pkg/agent (KnowledgeInvocationFingerprint) still refuses any non-allowlisted arg whenever opts.Knowledge is set, so an admitted launch stays fully controlled.

M1 rule:
- *service.CollaborationError: terminal with its code (knowledge_invocation_unsupported, knowledge_context_changed, knowledge_authorization_denied, and any code returned by RevalidateKnowledgeManifest).
- pgx.ErrNoRows (runtime, agent, chat, issue or autopilot row truly gone mid-claim): terminal, current reason kept.
- Settlement failure inside failClaimedTaskBeforeLaunch: keeps its existing requeue fallback.
- Every other error: immediate requeue and a 500. No failure_reason is written.
rationale:
Why safe-but-unlisted options get base execution and not refusal, with the gate on:
- Spec line 150: "Switch false / unsupported safe fresh runtime" maps to "No positive private negotiation; retain history guard and ordinary eligible base behavior".
- Spec line 164: "a safe unsupported backend retain base execution".
- Spec line 120: "unsupported options cannot claim it". Here "it" is the initial private support, meaning negotiation, not the task.
- Spec lines 89-90 reserve refusal for unsafe explicit selectors and for history that does not prove no exposure.
- The leaf's own doc (knowledge_launch.go:99-103) says ordinary legacy execution does not call the allowlist.
Refusing instead would make the allowlist a terminal kill switch for every claude agent the moment an operator enables the gate.

Why selector refusal ignores the gate:
- task.go:59-61 says historical-session safety checks remain active while the gate is disabled.
- Spec line 165 lists as bad: "reuse an exposed session after toggling the gate".
- Turning the gate off does not remove transcripts already on disk. The namespace guard cannot see exposure whose task rows were deleted, but an explicit --resume <id> or --continue can still reach it.
- Keeping this rule unchanged also preserves the existing guard test and the 'never silently strip' rule.

Why --no-session-persistence falls into the unsupported bucket and not a terminal refusal. Ordinary knowledge needs a persisted native session to bind for later resume, so it must never negotiate with this flag; validateTaskKnowledgeOrdinaryArgs keeps enforcing that. On a fresh unexposed task, base execution discloses nothing, so failing the task protects nothing. It also lets one daemon-wide MULTICA_CLAUDE_ARGS carry the collaboration contract without failing every ordinary claude task. Spec line 134 ("Ordinary resumable knowledge intentionally refuses this flag; do not merge the two policies") is still met, because negotiation refuses it and the collaboration policy is untouched.

Why M1 requeues. The neighboring branches requeue on transient errors. Requeue settles nothing and launches nothing, which is still fail closed. It keeps every knowledge column, so the next claim reruns the full history guard, and a retained negotiated row still refuses unsupported clients. A claim-time read failure before any descriptor is finalized is not one of the knowledge failure reasons that spec line 110 excludes from requeue.

changes.change: Add `func KnowledgeSessionSelectorPresent(provider string, args []string) bool`. It returns false for providers other than claude. For each raw token: arg := unshellQuoteArg(raw); name, _, _ := strings.Cut(arg, "="); return true if name has any prefix in {"--resume", "--continue", "--session", "--fork-session", "--from-pr"}, or if len(arg) > 1 && arg[0] == '-' && arg[1] != '-' && strings.ContainsAny(arg[1:], "cr"). The doc comment states that it scans values and tokens after "--" with no arity parsing, that it decides refusal for fallback, and that ValidateKnowledgeSessionArgs stays the only admission rule. Optionally point the ValidateKnowledgeSessionArgs comment at the new helper.

In BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim at line 357, replace `validateTaskKnowledgeOrdinaryArgs("claude", inv.ExtraArgs) != nil || validateTaskKnowledgeOrdinaryArgs("claude", custom) != nil` with `agent.KnowledgeSessionSelectorPresent("claude", inv.ExtraArgs) || agent.KnowledgeSessionSelectorPresent("claude", custom)`. Keep the malformed-custom_args refusal (lines 352-355). Add a comment: selectors are refused whatever the gate; other options only make the invocation unsupported. Leave taskKnowledgeInvocationSupported and validateTaskKnowledgeOrdinaryArgs unchanged; they still govern admission and still keep --no-session-persistence out of negotiation.

Add `func knowledgeClaimErrorDisposition(err error) (code string, requeue bool)`. It returns (domain.Code, false) when errors.As finds a *service.CollaborationError, ("knowledge_unavailable", false) when errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows), and ("", true) otherwise. In the BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim error branch (lines 3234-3241), when requeue is true: slog.Error("task claim: knowledge history load failed; requeueing claim", task_id, error), then call h.TaskService.RequeueTaskAfterClaimFailure(r.Context(), *task), logging a requeue failure as 'stale reclaim will recover it'. Then return &claimBuildFailure{outcome: "error_knowledge_claim_load", status: http.StatusInternalServerError, message: "failed to load task knowledge context"}. Otherwise keep the existing failClaimedTaskBeforeLaunch call with that code. The batch handler needs no change.

For a v1 Claude invocation, any daemon-default or agent custom argument that, after the same unshell-quoting as launch, is a `--resume*`, `--continue*`, `--session*`, `--fork-session*` or `--from-pr*` long option, or a single-dash cluster containing `c` or `r`, refuses with `knowledge_invocation_unsupported`. Values and tokens after `--` are scanned, and the selector is never stripped. Any other option outside the negotiation allowlist only makes the invocation unsupported, and the history guard below then chooses base execution or refusal."

Line 108-110 paragraph. After "All knowledge failure reasons are excluded from automatic fresh fallback, requeue and input replay." add: "A transient dependency read while building a claim, before any descriptor is finalized, is not a knowledge failure reason."

Lines 133-134. Replace "Ordinary resumable knowledge intentionally refuses this flag; do not merge the two policies." with: "Ordinary resumable knowledge never negotiates with this flag: a fresh unexposed task takes base execution, while a retained negotiated task or a leaf launch carrying knowledge intent refuses with `knowledge_invocation_unsupported`. Do not merge the two policies."

Section 4 matrix. Line 150: change the condition to "Switch false / unsupported safe fresh runtime (including safe options outside the negotiation allowlist and ordinary `--no-session-persistence`)". After line 154, add the row: "Transient read failure while building a claim, before descriptor finalization | Requeue that exact claim generation with no failure reason; typed refusals and missing rows stay terminal".

Line 69 (`knowledge_invocation_unsupported` row). Add: "Options outside the negotiation allowlist, such as `--allowedTools` or `--add-dir`, no longer fail fresh tasks; those tasks run without knowledge. Session selectors such as `--continue` and `--resume` still refuse."

compatibility_and_risks:
Legacy daemons that send no inv are unchanged. v1 daemons on the default deployment (gate off) stop terminally failing claude tasks whose daemon defaults or custom_args contain options the allowlist does not list. Selector configs such as --continue still refuse on v1, as they do today. With the gate on, unlisted options and --no-session-persistence now run base execution without knowledge, where they used to refuse. An operator who expects knowledge in that configuration gets no descriptor and no error, so observability may be worth a follow-up.

The selector denylist is coarse on purpose. Some harmless values refuse, but HEAD refuses them too, so nothing regresses. A future Claude selector with a new name would pass the gate-off v1 fallback; the namespace history guard and the leaf allowlist still bound it.

M1: a persistent error that is neither a domain error nor NoRows would requeue and wake the runtime on every poll. The agent-load branch already carries the same risk; M1-B (stale reclaim) is the fallback if that matters. When the request context is cancelled, the requeue itself fails and the stale reclaim recovers the task. The requeue SQL leaves knowledge columns intact, so retained negotiation and recorded exposure survive.

Testing: every DB-backed test needs the explicit isolated database (.trellis/spec/server/database-test-isolation.md). newTaskKnowledgeHTTPFixture calls t.Fatal without one, and other handler DB tests skip silently. The handler fault test mutates the shared testHandler.TaskService.Queries, so it must not run in parallel.

This is a design only. Nothing was built, vetted or run in this pass.
open_questions: Legacy daemons (inv == nil) whose custom_args contain --continue or --resume are not refused by step 1, and the server cannot see their daemon defaults. Closing this would change old-daemon behavior that spec line 91 says to preserve, so it needs an owner decision. It is out of scope for H1.

Should --no-session-persistence with the gate on take base execution (chosen) or keep a terminal refusal? The refusal reading treats spec line 134 as task-level, and keeping it means a one-line gate-on branch and the original test.
Should a gate-on claim that falls back to base because of an unlisted option emit a log or metric, so operators can see why knowledge was not delivered?

pgx.ErrNoRows keeps the knowledge_unavailable reason for unrelated tasks (for example codex). Relabeling it to invalid_task_identity, as the agent-load branch does, would be clearer, but RevalidateKnowledgeManifest might also return NoRows, so it was left unchanged.

Adjacent and unverified: the FinalizeTaskClaim error branch (daemon.go ~3584-3594) always requeues, including domain refusals from finalizeTaskKnowledgeClaim such as knowledge_context_changed when the 32-claim bound is hit. That could requeue repeatedly instead of failing. It is outside H1/M1 and was not traced end-to-end.
